source.title: Billion-Scale Graph Foundation Models
source.authors: Maya Bechler-Speicher; Yoel Gottlieb; A. Isakov; David Abensur; A. Tavory; Daniel Haimovich; Ido Guy; Udi Weinsberg

record.tranche_reason: Applies scaling-law measurements to graph foundation models, a different modality and pretraining objective from language-model scaling.
record.gate_note: Section 6 reports the study's own validation-loss scaling sweep and fitted exponents. Downstream-task results, architecture ablations, and cited language-model scaling results do not measure the claim versions cataloged here.
record.test_reason: Section 6 fits Kaplan's joint L(N,D) power-law form to the study's own validation loss. The sweep covers nine model sizes (1e6 to 4e9 parameters) and eight data sizes (3e5 to 1e9 edges) for a graph transformer trained with masked link prediction. This is a new modality and objective, so the results bear on V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that GraphBFF validation loss follows Kaplan-form power laws in model and data size, with model and data bottlenecks, so the two must be scaled jointly. They caution that the laws come from one Enterprise dataset and may not transfer to graphs with different degree distributions or feature spaces. They also say compute-optimal allocation remains open for graph models.
record.recipe_differences: Graph-model scaling on an Enterprise graph with masked link prediction and validation loss, rather than language-model pretraining with token-based cross-entropy scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper states that scaling laws may not transfer to graphs with different degree distributions or feature spaces; compute-optimal conclusions depend on the graph and sampling distribution.
record.problems: The scaling laws are measured on one Enterprise dataset and the text cautions against assuming transfer to graphs with different distributions. The paper does not report uncertainty for the fitted exponents or an out-of-fit extrapolation test.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant scaling results left out. Downstream task evaluations and attention-component ablations do not measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: Only a single heterogeneous Enterprise graph with masked link prediction. Image or video models, repeated-data regimes, fine-tuning and transfer scaling are not tested.
The laws are fitted on the full sweep. No small-run fit is evaluated against held-out larger runs.
No compute-optimal allocation is derived. The authors call it an open problem because compute is graph-conditional.
Downstream tasks are evaluated for only one 1.4B model and are not related to scale or loss.
No comparison of shape at fixed parameter count. The TCA/TAA ablation is a component ablation on downstream tasks.
No comparison of fitting methods, schedules or parameter counting.

missing.what: Joint five-parameter fit of L(N,D), including the irreducible loss L∞, over the full N×D grid (Fig. 4c). The fitted L∞ value and the goodness of fit are not reported numerically.
Statement that larger GFMs reach a given test loss with fewer training examples (sample efficiency with scale), as in Kaplan et al.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V5 limits_scope label was dropped. It rested on untested settings and the authors' caution about transfer, not on any result showing the power law failing, and untested parts belong under untested. The fitted exponents differ greatly from LM values (alpha_N 0.703 vs Kaplan's ~0.076). This bears on exponent values, not on the form that V5 claims. No uncertainty on the fits is reported, and the data are a single proprietary graph. The fit is on the early-stopped best validation loss with four learning rates per configuration.

versions.untested_parts: Tests graph-model loss scaling, not held-out pretraining loss of language models.
Fits scaling curves over the sweep, but does not report fitting on small runs and then evaluating predictions on substantially larger runs held out from fitting.
Does not measure a compute-optimal parameter/data allocation or its growth with compute. It states that compute-optimal allocation for graph models remains open.
Does not compare depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count in the scaling sweep.
Tests one graph modality, one enterprise dataset, and masked link prediction. It does not test image or video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling laws.
Downstream results are not related to a sweep of pretraining loss or scale.

Does not vary fitting methods, data, or training schedules to compare fitted exponents, or report curves bending away from a power law. It notes that compute-optimal conclusions for graph models are graph-conditional.

rows.subject: GraphBFF Transformer
rows.size_stated: Nine model sizes spanning 106 to 4 × 109 parameters
rows.operation_detail: Swept model size and measured validation loss on a fixed holdout of approximately 6 million edges; fitted the model-limited loss curve.

conditions.value: Sufficiently large datasets; data sizes in the sweep ranged from 3 × 105 to 109 supervision edges
Validation loss for masked link prediction

rows.value: For models trained to convergence on sufficiently large datasets, αN ≈ 0.703 and Nc ≈ 2.1 × 104; the paper reports a power-law decrease in loss with model size.
rows.note: The model-size sweep spans four orders of magnitude. The paper reports validation loss, not language-model cross-entropy.
rows.check: Size and data ranges are garbled: '106 to 4 × 109' should read 10^6 to 4×10^9 parameters, and '3 × 105 to 109' should read 3×10^5 to 10^9 edges. The measure is early-stopped validation BCE loss on a ~6M-edge holdout. No baseline or uncertainty is given. Otherwise correct.

rows.subject: GraphBFF Transformer
rows.size_stated: Nine model sizes spanning 106 to 4 × 109 parameters
rows.operation_detail: Swept training-data size and measured validation loss on a fixed holdout of approximately 6 million edges; fitted the data-limited loss curve.

conditions.value: Sufficiently large models; model sizes in the sweep ranged from 106 to 4 × 109 parameters
Validation loss for masked link prediction

rows.value: For large enough models trained with a limited dataset size, αD ≈ 0.188 and Dc ≈ 4.7; the paper reports a power-law decrease in loss with data size.
rows.note: The data-size sweep spans five orders of magnitude. The paper reports validation loss, not language-model cross-entropy.
rows.check: Same exponent-notation garbling of the size ranges as r1. The fit reports alpha_D≈0.188 and Dc≈4.7 and is otherwise correct. The paper reports saturation at fixed N, which fits the joint form rather than contradicting it.

relationships.condition: GraphBFF Transformer, Enterprise heterogeneous graph, masked link prediction, early-stopped validation loss
relationships.reason: Validation loss follows the fitted Kaplan power-law form in model size (r1, alpha_N≈0.703) and data size (r2, alpha_D≈0.188) across 4–5 orders of magnitude.
relationships.display_finding: Kaplan-form fits give model-size exponent about 0.703 and data-size exponent about 0.188 across four to five orders of magnitude.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
